title: Working carnivals and fairs with Joe Roverson
summary: Vincent describes road carnival and fair work, band size, and the 49 dance where three bands alternated.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Ask him who he worked in carnivals with. Carnival?

Yeah. He said, who you worked with in carnival? Who? You. Well, my band never was thick as ever on the kind of walking. The last kind of, well, I was still hired. They're taking a job bass band. So I couldn't make it. Romain Emphries was with us then. They said that night we played at the Benitez Hall. It was Benitez, no, the Italian Hall. Espelette out in there. Dauphin, ain't it? Rumpel. Rumpel, yeah. He played that that night. You know that old man said, you know, never want to take no parade away. He didn't walk out there. He just paid for the budget, you know.
Tell him how mean those road carnivals, the way you went out on the road. Oh.

He said he mean them road carnivals when you went out on the road? Oh, you mean in the carnival? Yeah. Oh, I said you mean carnival, yeah, carnival. Oh, me and Joe Roverson, Hothead, you know, different fellas like that I was with, you know.
You asked me how big a band they used.

How big a band would you have? Well, we had, let me see, a left fella named Herman, Jim, Jim Kelly, I played, my son. He didn't have playing drums. I didn't have Joe Stettick playing drums. And then when I went away with the kids, with Wesley Don, he used to play my band then. And the rest of the time, Joe Roverson was a piano player, you know. And, uh, my father, I see him. It seemed to really get kind of a band that time. They had a dance that called the 49 dance. It was three bands, you see. We played an hour and a half, knock off the other band, play an hour and a half, knock the other one. Then we'd go around different places on the ground and play. But, uh, we and I too were together. But we had that, uh, that wasn't no, that was a fair what we had. We couldn't turn down at a day and turn down at a night, you see. That was a fair, that wasn't no comedy, you see. And that's where I came back there when I was with Joe Roverson and I came back there to get some clover. And when I went back, we went and they started playing our band. And we jumped. And Joe went to clean all the two and I'm all up there and in the noise, you know. But they come back there, raggedy, pukorn. Raggedy what?
Raggedy as a pukorn. Yeah. Yeah.
And then I fell, I guess, I was like that, but it took the railroad from home and all that.
